answer: Reputation-decayed admission pricing. Each new identity's entry price scales with the ocean of unproven accounts created in the last window: more births, higher cost. A mirror check links registration metadata (IP, timing, device) so near-duplicates pay a multiplied fee. Costs decay only through sustained, distinct activity—like a sparrow returning seasonally—so mass registration pays steeply per head, while a lone legitimate user pays little once history accrues.
